title: My Claude Code horror game ran fine on desktop but was broken on every phone. The game was measuring its own screen wrong.
author: Happy_Literature_194
selftext:
A few weeks ago I released Wake Word: Almost Home, a free browser horror game where you watch a family through 9 security cameras, and one of them isn't who they say they are. I built it with Claude Code, and the art came from ChatGPT.

Players kept telling me they play on their phones, so I made a mobile version. The main bug was surprising: on phones, the game miscalculated its own viewport, so the top and bottom were cut off and all the text rendered at half size.

What I changed for mobile:  
\- Fixed the viewport, and made text and monitors about 1.5x bigger  
\- Moved the side panels into tabs (Listen, Sensors, Basement)  
\- The Listen tab opens automatically when someone makes a request  
\- The Basement tab blinks red when something needs you  
\- A "turn your phone" screen pauses the game in portrait  
\- Rewrote the tutorial for touch, in English and Persian

Testing: I had Claude play full nights in a simulated phone screen using taps only, and it reached the true ending with zero console errors.

It's free, no download, 4 endings:  
https://redrakam.itch.io/wake-word-almost-home

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
